format: Edited step walkthrough from actual Windows CI UI captures; no continuous screen recording; report header and preview table use documented detail crops
fixture_note: Only the first server substitutes a fictional fixed receipt ID and UTC time for repeatability. All API tokens remain random and private. Runtime files are unchanged.

chapters.title: Begin with a known result
chapters.caption: The default due-date report starts with invented work orders. No CSV has been imported.
chapters.note: Check the starting point before changing the dataset.

chapters.title: Preview before writing
chapters.caption: Load the included synthetic sample and inspect every row. Preview leaves the report at nine orders.
chapters.note: All rows must pass. Apply is a separate, explicit action.

chapters.title: Commit the orders and receipt together
chapters.caption: Apply adds three orders and two completion events. Their receipt commits in the same SQLite transaction.
chapters.note: If receipt storage fails, the whole import rolls back.

chapters.title: Inspect the stored explanation
chapters.caption: View the saved receipt and download its exact JSON bytes. Raw CSV contents and filenames are not stored.
chapters.note: The displayed ID and time are fixed fictional capture fixtures.

chapters.title: Restart the app; reopen the receipt
chapters.caption: The original app process stops. A new process opens the same database and downloads the identical receipt.
chapters.note: The browser download bytes match the first download exactly.

chapters.title: Restore into a fresh directory
chapters.caption: Stop the app, back up, verify and restore with the CLI. Reopen the new copy and download the receipt again.
chapters.note: This is local history, not a signed audit log or a power-loss guarantee.
